newsitem.title: USA: N.J. Senate panel sets utility tax hearing Wed.
newsitem.headline: N.J. Senate panel sets utility tax hearing Wed.

text.p: A New Jersey Senate committee scheduled public hearings for Wednesday on a bill to eliminate the different tax treatments for utility and non-utility energy providers, a committee representative said Tuesday.

The Senate Budget and Appropriations Committee will hear testimony on the bill, which is designed to spur competition in the state's utility market. Senate Republicans said the legislation could cut costs to ratepayers by about 45 percent.

Senate President Donald DiFrancesco said it is an attempt to update New Jersey's "antiquated energy tax structure in order to promote fairer competition among utilities, to stem losses we have incurred as a state because of our high energy rates, and to ensure that both commercial and residential consumers benefit from the revolution that is occurring in the utilities market."

DiFrancesco said he would testify Wednesday, as would Board of Public Utilities President Herbert Tate. Other participants are expected to include municipal government representatives and officials of utility companies.
